meta.title: Emberwood
meta.goal: Relight the Keeper's road and out-argue Vespera at Ashen Peak to wake the Great Hearth — then answer whatever wakes up with it.

commands.text: That's a good little flame you've got there. North for the Trail — brazier first, then Mosshollow.
No one walks the Trail without a kindred, love. Maren's kiln is the stone house west — go choose yours.
The kiln-hearth crackles like it's pleased with itself. Your kindred lean into the warmth.
Woof! (Biscuit smells of warm bread and rain, and is very pleased about something.)
Two Keeper's marks, and the kettle sang all morning. Go finish it, love.
Fern's mark already? Your mother would have burst her buttons.
The kettle's gone cold twice this week with a fire under it. Kettles don't do that.
KILNHEARTH — feed the dog, mind the kettle, keep the fire.
Six! I taught forty years and never once filled the whole hearth-side.
Take these. A full party eats a great deal of salve.
Relight the Trail brazier first; the road remembers the rest. And if you meet Vespera up there... be kind before you're clever.
The Trail brazier guttered out this morning, and my knees won't make the climb. Three young kindred wait by the north wall — warm your hands and choose one.
The emberling hops off its pedestal before you've finished reaching. A coal with opinions, this one.
The pedestal is warm where the emberling sat.
The puddlit pours itself into your hands, then reshapes, pleased. It will follow you home now; that's simply what it does.
A damp ring marks where the puddlit waited.
The sproutle grabs your sleeve with one leafy hand and does not let go. It has been sleeping in this plant pot all winter.
An empty plant pot, still faintly warm.
This paddock's for the odd ones — kindred that wandered in from nowhere anybody knows. Nobody here asks where from.
Step into the grass if you like. Whatever's living in it today is still finding its feet, same as you.
The brazier holds its small flame against the grey. Your kindred lean in.
The waystone brazier is cold, its ash fine as flour. You rake the coals, strike your firebox, and coax it back.
Warmth rolls down the Trail like something let out of a jar. Somewhere south, a kettle sings.

trainer.intro: You walk like you've somewhere to be. Nobody's got somewhere to be anymore.
trainer.defeatText: Huh. Maybe somewhere's worth walking to after all.
trainer.outro: Mind the grass past the bend — it rustles even when the wind doesn't.

trainer.intro: Hold up — my two haven't stretched their legs since the frost came.
trainer.defeatText: Well scrapped. Warm work is good work.
trainer.outro: The brazier went dark on my watch, and I hate that. Glad someone's climbing.

trainer.intro: Shh, you'll scare the voltpup. Ah — too late, fight me.
trainer.defeatText: Fair's fair. The pup likes you, which is annoying.
trainer.outro: Voltpups nest in the east grass. Bring a snare and patience.

commands.text: VERDANT TRAIL — the grass is lively; travelers keep a snare handy.
Fern's mark, plain as morning. The Ascent is open to you — mind the vents.
The high road stays shut till a Keeper vouches for you. Fern keeps her grove southeast, past the market.
Embersalve, ten coins the jar — kiln-warm, mind your fingers.
Great embersalve, thirty coins — for the hurt you can't walk off.
Kindling snares, twenty — the weave takes best on a tired kindred.
Warm snares, forty-five — the good weave, holds heat and patience.
The town hearth burns low and steady, ringed with drying socks. Your kindred settle into the warmth.

trainer.intro: Maren sent you? Then show me she taught you more than kindling.
trainer.defeatText: There it is — the stubbornness the road needs. Take my mark, and warm snares in place of the charm; the charms won't hold their heat anymore.
trainer.outro: The marsh folk say the west reeds are lonely. Kindred hate lonely.

commands.text: The hives hummed today — first time since autumn. Whatever you're doing up there, don't stop.
Fern vouches for you, so I'll say it plain: the bees stopped humming, and I'm frightened.
Quiet hives. Bees don't hum when they're cold, and nothing's colder than this spring.
My bee pasture west of here is full of Flufflehups — all ears and eyes and burr-tails. Wade in, they don't bite.
MOSSHOLLOW — market row north, Keeper Fern's grove southeast. The hearth is free, always.
She'll sing when the fog rolls in. Let her.
You smell of woodsmoke — proper smoke, Trail smoke. Then you'll do.
Her name's her own business, but she answers to Wick. Keep her out of the wind.
Cold hands, cold lantern. Light the Trail brazier and we'll talk.

trainer.intro: Fog's thick enough to lean on today. Let's see if your kindred keep their footing.
trainer.defeatText: Sure-footed after all. Take the coins before they rust.
trainer.outro: The old one in the west reeds doesn't care for strangers. Trail smoke on your coat might change his mind.

commands.text: A grey heron stands in the shallows, doing nothing loudly.

trainer.intro: Ironwood's gate taught me to stand still; this mountain taught me why. Show me your flame, traveler.
trainer.defeatText: Ha — you'd have talked your way past my old gate too. Go up, and don't let the quiet fool you.
trainer.outro: I still say 'the elder sends her blessing' in my sleep. Don't tell Fern.

trainer.intro: The vents are running cold, and cold vents make me nervous. Prove you're worth the worry.
trainer.defeatText: Warm hands, warm heart, whatever. Go on up.
trainer.outro: Cindertails sleep in the warm gravel. Step soft and carry a snare.

trainer.intro: Rockfall took the path twice this month. My pebblor and I put it back — twice.
trainer.defeatText: Solid work. Bram will want a look at you.
trainer.outro: Keeper Bram holds the high gate. Softer than the mountain, but not by much.

commands.text: CINDER ASCENT — the vents run warm underfoot, or used to. Keeper Bram holds the high gate.

rewardCommands.text: Then grieve loud, all of you. Perhaps that was the braver way to keep a fire.
Vespera says nothing for a long while. Then she hands you the long iron, and steps aside.

lines: You touch the iron to the banked coals and the Great Hearth catches with a sound
like the valley exhaling. Morning comes up loud — birdsong, geyser-hiss, kettles
knocking, and far below, Biscuit barking at all of it.

rewardCommands.text: Vespera: "...that shouldn't be possible. Something down there is answering it."
At the east end of the summit, a wall of cooled slag cracks from the inside.
The slag at the east end of the summit has opened. Go down.

trainer.intro: You relit them. Even knowing everything goes out, you relit them.

commands.text: Go home and be loud about it. I will keep the fire honest up here.
East end. Whatever is down there has been waiting longer than I was.
The Great Hearth roars, young again. The whole mountain hums like a struck bell.
The Great Hearth, banked coal by coal to a whisper. It is not out — it is waiting.
A little hearth, still lit, swept daily. Someone up here keeps one fire against the dark.
Long cold. When you lean close, something pale flutters up out of the ash.
Scratched into the rim, old and shallow: 'V & T'. You leave it be.
The slag has cracked open. Warm air comes up from somewhere far below.
A wall of cooled slag, cold as everything else up here.
It sleeps warm instead of cold. That is all any of us wanted.
I banked the Hearth for years and never once came down here. I was afraid of what I'd find still burning.
The first fire. Older than the braziers, older than Keepers. It has been alone a long time.
Go down through the ember veins and find the first fire.
No. You relit them; you should be the one it meets.
But take this. It was my snare, once, and I was better at catching than at keeping.
Go down through the ember veins and find the first fire.
No. But I am warm, and the difference turns out to matter.
The fire here has never once gone out.

trainer.intro: Nobody comes down here. You're either lost or you're the one who relit it.
trainer.defeatText: The one who relit it, then.

commands.text: Keep to the veins. The heat reads your intentions.
The Hearth-Mouth
commands.subtitle: under the Great Hearth

commands.text: Warm air moves up past you, going the wrong way for a cave.
Explore the Underhearth. Talk to Vespera.

trainer.intro: Mind the dark ones. They don't bite. They just make you forget why you came.

commands.text: Straight up the middle and you'll reach the old chamber.

trainer.intro: Everyone stops here. Nobody's gone past me yet.

commands.text: Go on up. It's been waiting longer than any of us.
Someone banked these coals neatly, a long time ago.
The Ember Veins
The tubes glow faintly from within, like something breathing slowly.
Climb the ember veins to the old chamber at the top.

rewardCommands.title: The First Hearth
lines: It had been alone under the mountain since before there were braziers to bank,
keeping itself small so that it would last.
That is what Vespera had been doing too, in her way, and neither of them
had been able to say so out loud.
You bank your own fire beside it, the way you were taught on the first morning,
and leave it burning at a size it does not have to be careful about.

rewardCommands.text: The Underhearth comes up bright behind you all the way to the surface, and the valley — already awake — gets warmer without anyone being able to say why.

commands.text: The First Hearth
Something enormous is banked at the far end of the chamber, glowing low.
It does not speak. It banks itself lower, the way a dog lowers its head, and the whole chamber dims.
Meet the first fire.
